comments.author: stanfordkid
comments.text:
I find the discussion here to be slightly myopic. It is obvious he did something wrong, it is also obvious that members of the government and other actors likely knew about all of this for several years. You aren't the CEO of a trillion dollar company without being under the eye of many people. The real question people should be asking is "why now?" why is the PR spectacle happening at this moment and who is benefitting from supplying the NYTimes with this compromising information.
Obviously we can only come up with conjecture, but it should at least be discussed that this is not happening out of thin air due solely to his reckless actions but represents some kind of hidden power struggle. It's quite clear to me folks like Secretary of State Marco Rubio very likely
knew
about these things taking place for quite some time.

comments.author: irishloop
comments.text:
I think a lot of people here seem to underestimate how much of a CEO's job is perception.
"Oh who cares who he slept with, he's been great for Nvidia. Nothing has been proven."
He's one of the most visible CEO's in the most visible industry in the world, and the entire AI economy is dependent upon them. The perception of him as stable is incredibly important.
Merely the suggestion that he is having affairs with people with close ties to China's government, given export controls, is a huge PR problem. Adding in an additional affair with someone under him. And the likelihood that there may be even more out there.
I doubt the Board wants to get rid of Jensen Huang. He's done incredibly well for them. But right now, there's a huge PR shitstorm swirling around the company.
Maybe in six months it all dies down and he comes back, who knows. But right now, you really can't just ignore the problem and hope the media doesn't care about the whole "well she was only sort of a spy" situation.
